spectral.true_color: High confidence: dark green woodland dominates. Central openings range from muted green to pale tan, while the large central-left opening is brown. Narrow corridors are pale gray to nearly white. Strong local contrasts occur at woodland–opening boundaries.
spectral.false_color: High confidence: much of the woody cover becomes bright or deep red. Central herbaceous openings are generally muted pink or reddish gray. The brown central-left clearing becomes green-gray, with scattered darker or reddish spots. Pale corridors appear cyan-white. Some right-hand woodland blocks remain comparatively dark red.

implications.claim: The extensive red response supports widespread photosynthetically active vegetation, although displayed redness is not a calibrated measure of vigor.
The central-left clearing has less green vegetation cover or a weaker vegetation response than surrounding woodland; exposed soil, dry vegetation, and disturbance remain competing explanations.
Muted red in central openings may reflect lower canopy density, shorter vegetation, senescence, or greater soil contribution.
Differences among red woodland blocks may reflect canopy type, density, age, or illumination; they do not independently establish plant stress.
Cyan-white narrow lines are consistent with exposed or constructed surfaces, but their color alone cannot distinguish tracks from some drainage features.
Neither soil moisture nor canopy water content can be reliably ranked from these display colors alone.
No confidently identified open-water body is available for assessing turbidity.

spectral.not_revealed: High confidence: these renderings do not provide calibrated reflectance, quantitative vegetation indices, soil or canopy moisture, water turbidity, crop species, tree species, canopy height, stand age, road material, or temporal change. Display stretches and mixed pixels limit comparisons of apparent brightness.
